q: Under Section 26 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the appropriate Government may, to the extent of availability of financial and other resources, among other things:

options.A: Decide the appeals preferred against the orders of the Central Public Information Officers
options.B: Fix the fee payable by applicants for obtaining information
options.C: Appoint the Central Public Information Officers in all public authorities
options.D: Develop and organise educational programmes for the public to advance their understanding of how to exercise the rights contemplated under the Act, encourage public authorities to participate in such programmes, and promote the training of Public Information Officers

e: Section 26 of the RTI Act, 2005 casts a role on the appropriate Government to develop and organise educational programmes to advance public understanding of the rights under the Act, encourage public authority participation, and promote training of Public Information Officers.

q: The Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968 do NOT apply to:

options.A: Non-gazetted railway servants in Group 'C'
options.B: Gazetted railway officers
options.C: Members of the Railway Protection Force
options.D: Railway servants serving on foreign service

e: The Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968 do not apply to members of the Railway Protection Force, who are governed by the RPF Act and the RPF Rules for disciplinary matters instead.

q: Under Section 106 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no court shall take cognizance of any offence under the Act unless a complaint thereof is made within the following period from the date on which the alleged commission of the offence came to the knowledge of an Inspector:

options.A: One month
options.B: Three months
options.C: Six months
options.D: One year

e: Section 106 of the Factories Act, 1948 bars a court from taking cognizance of an offence unless the complaint is made within three months of the date on which the alleged commission of the offence came to the knowledge of an Inspector.

q: Training Allowance admissible, under the 7th CPC dispensation, to the faculty members (instructors) posted in the training institutions of the Railways, other than the national academies, is payable at the rate of:

options.A: 12 per cent of basic pay
options.B: 24 per cent of basic pay
options.C: 10 per cent of basic pay
options.D: 30 per cent of basic pay

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, Training Allowance for faculty members in railway training institutions other than the national academies is payable at 12 per cent of basic pay; the higher 24 per cent rate is for the national academies.

q: For filling a selection post within Group 'C' on the Railways by departmental selection, the field of consideration (zone of consideration) among the senior-most eligible staff is ordinarily:

options.A: Equal to the number of vacancies to be filled
options.B: Twice the number of vacancies to be filled
options.C: Five times the number of vacancies to be filled
options.D: Three times the number of vacancies to be filled

e: For filling a selection post in Group C by departmental selection, the field of consideration among the senior-most eligible staff is ordinarily three times the number of vacancies to be filled, under the IREM selection instructions.

q: Under Section 105 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no court shall take cognizance of any offence under the Act except on a complaint made by, or with the previous sanction in writing of:

options.A: The District Magistrate of the district
options.B: The occupier of the factory
options.C: An Inspector of Factories
options.D: Any worker employed in the factory

e: Section 105 of the Factories Act, 1948 provides that no court shall take cognizance of an offence under the Act except on a complaint made by, or with the previous sanction in writing of, an Inspector of Factories.

q: In direct recruitment to posts on the Railways, the relaxation in the upper age limit admissible to widows, divorced women and women judicially separated from their husbands, who have not remarried, extends, in the case of candidates of the general category, up to the age of:

options.A: 30 years
options.B: 35 years
options.C: 38 years
options.D: 40 years

e: In direct recruitment, widows, divorced women and women judicially separated from their husbands who have not remarried get relaxation in the upper age limit up to 35 years of age in the case of general category candidates.

q: 'Hazardous process', as defined in the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, means any process or activity in relation to an industry specified in the First Schedule to the Act, where, unless special care is taken, the raw materials used therein or the intermediate or finished products, bye-products, wastes or effluents thereof would:

options.A: Cause material impairment to the health of the persons engaged in or connected therewith, or result in the pollution of the general environment
options.B: Merely increase the cost of production of the factory
options.C: Require the employment of a larger number of workers in the factory
options.D: Require the previous sanction of the Railway Board for carrying it on

e: Section 2(cb) of the Factories Act, 1948 defines a hazardous process as one in the First Schedule industries where, unless special care is taken, the materials, products, wastes or effluents would cause material impairment to health or pollute the general environment.

q: Encashment of Leave on Average Pay by a railway servant in conjunction with Leave Travel Concession is admissible subject to the condition that, after such encashment, the balance of Leave on Average Pay at his credit shall not be less than:

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: No minimum balance is required to be maintained

e: Encashment of Leave on Average Pay along with LTC is allowed only up to the prescribed limit and subject to the condition that the balance of LAP at credit after the encashment is not less than 30 days, under the Railway Services leave instructions.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation in promotion in railway services:
1. Reservation in promotion is admissible to candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
2. Reservation in promotion is also admissible to candidates belonging to the Other Backward Classes.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Reservation in promotion in railway services is admissible to SC and ST candidates under the constitutional and DoPT instructions applied on the Railways. There is no reservation in promotion for OBC candidates, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Under Section 11 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, where the walls and ceilings of a workroom in a factory are whitewashed or colourwashed, the whitewashing or colourwashing is required to be repeated once in every:

options.A: Six months
options.B: Twelve months
options.C: Fourteen months
options.D: Twenty-four months

e: Section 11 of the Factories Act, 1948 prescribes cleanliness standards: where walls and ceilings are whitewashed or colourwashed, the whitewashing or colourwashing must be repeated once in every fourteen months.

q: Under Section 12(3) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the Chief Information Commissioner and the Information Commissioners are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee consisting of:

options.A: The Chief Justice of India, the Prime Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
options.B: The Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
options.C: The Vice-President, the Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
options.D: The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha as Chairperson, the Prime Minister and the Home Minister

e: Section 12(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 provides for appointment of the CIC and Information Commissioners by the President on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

q: For appointment to a post in railway service, a candidate who is not a citizen of India may yet be eligible for appointment if he is:

options.A: A subject of Nepal or of Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came over to India before the 1st January, 1962, and holds a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India
options.B: A citizen of any Commonwealth country, without any certificate
options.C: A foreign national residing in India for more than one year
options.D: A person holding an Overseas Citizen of India card, without any further condition

e: A non-citizen may be eligible for railway appointment if he is a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1st January 1962, and holds a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India.

q: Under Section 29 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, every lifting machine (other than a hoist or lift), chain, rope and lifting tackle in a factory shall be thoroughly examined by a competent person at least:

options.A: Once in every month
options.B: Once in every three months
options.C: Once in every six months
options.D: Once in every twelve months

e: Section 29 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires every lifting machine other than a hoist or lift, and every chain, rope and lifting tackle, to be thoroughly examined by a competent person at least once in every twelve months.

q: Under Section 3 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the responsibility for the payment of all wages required to be paid under the Act to persons employed by him rests on:

options.A: The Accounts Officer of the establishment
options.B: The employer
options.C: The Inspector appointed under the Act
options.D: The recognised trade union of the establishment

e: Section 3 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 fixes responsibility for payment of all wages required to be paid under the Act on the employer, including where a contractor or a person designated by the employer is involved.

q: Under Section 80 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a worker who is allowed leave with wages is entitled to wages for the leave period at a rate equal to:

options.A: One-half of his average daily earnings in the preceding month
options.B: His wages for the last day worked before the leave
options.C: The daily average of his total full-time earnings for the days on which he actually worked during the month immediately preceding his leave
options.D: A fixed rate prescribed by the Railway Board for all factories

e: Section 80 of the Factories Act, 1948 entitles a worker allowed leave with wages to wages at a rate equal to the daily average of his total full-time earnings for the days actually worked during the month immediately preceding his leave.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 19 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 44,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twenty times the emoluments, as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death after 19 years falls in the 11-20 years slab, so death gratuity is 20 x emoluments under the RS (Pension) Rules. Computation: 20 x Rs 44,000 = Rs 8,80,000.

q: Under the Apprentices Act, 1961, a person shall not be qualified to be engaged as an apprentice to undergo apprenticeship training in a designated trade unless he:

options.A: Has completed the age of sixteen years in every case
options.B: Has completed the age of fifteen years in every case
options.C: Has completed the age of eighteen years in every case
options.D: Is not less than fourteen years of age and satisfies the prescribed standards of education and physical fitness

e: Section 3 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 qualifies a person for engagement as an apprentice if he is not less than fourteen years of age and satisfies the prescribed standards of education and physical fitness for the trade.

q: Under Section 4(1)(a) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, every public authority is required to maintain all its records:

options.A: Only in paper form in the record room of the authority
options.B: Duly catalogued and indexed in a manner which facilitates the right to information, and to ensure that the records are computerised within a reasonable time, subject to the availability of resources
options.C: Only for a period of five years from the date of their creation
options.D: In the personal custody of the head of the office

e: Section 4(1)(a) of the RTI Act, 2005 requires every public authority to maintain all its records duly catalogued and indexed in a manner facilitating the right to information, and to computerise them within a reasonable time subject to availability of resources.

q: Under Section 36 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no person shall be allowed to enter any chamber, tank, pit or other confined space in a factory in which dangerous fumes are likely to be present, unless:

options.A: He is a member of a recognised trade union
options.B: He has completed ten years of service in the factory
options.C: He is accompanied by the occupier of the factory
options.D: It has been certified in writing by a competent person that the space is free from dangerous fumes and safe for entry, or the prescribed protective measures have been taken

e: Section 36 of the Factories Act, 1948 bars entry into a confined space where dangerous fumes are likely unless it has been certified in writing by a competent person as free from dangerous fumes and safe for entry, or the prescribed protective measures have been taken.

q: In regard to a railway servant who has been placed under suspension, the correct position is that he:

options.A: May leave his headquarters freely at any time during the suspension
options.B: Is deemed to be on leave for the whole period of suspension
options.C: Shall not leave his headquarters without obtaining the prior permission of the authority which placed him under suspension
options.D: Must report daily to the police station of the area

e: A railway servant under suspension is not deemed to be on leave and remains subject to control: he shall not leave his headquarters without obtaining the prior permission of the authority which placed him under suspension.

q: Under Section 10 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, a claim for compensation shall not be entertained by the Commissioner unless notice of the accident has been given as soon as practicable and the claim is preferred before the Commissioner within:

options.A: Six months of the occurrence of the accident, or of the death of the employee
options.B: Two years of the occurrence of the accident, or of the death of the employee
options.C: One year of the occurrence of the accident, or of the death of the employee
options.D: Three years of the occurrence of the accident, or of the death of the employee

e: Section 10 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 requires notice of the accident as soon as practicable and the claim to be preferred before the Commissioner within two years of the accident or, in case of death, within two years of the death.

q: Under Section 111 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a worker in a factory shall not:

options.A: Report an accident in the factory to the Inspector of Factories
options.B: Ask for the display of the abstracts of the Act in the factory
options.C: Avail the leave with wages admissible to him under the Act
options.D: Wilfully interfere with, or misuse, any appliance, convenience or other thing provided in the factory for securing the health, safety or welfare of the workers

e: Section 111 of the Factories Act, 1948 lists workers' obligations, including that a worker shall not wilfully interfere with or misuse any appliance, convenience or other thing provided for securing the health, safety or welfare of workers.

q: Under Section 7(8) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, where a request for information is rejected, the Central Public Information Officer shall communicate to the person making the request:

options.A: The reasons for the rejection, the period within which an appeal against the rejection may be preferred, and the particulars of the appellate authority
options.B: Only the fact of rejection, without any reasons
options.C: The name of the officer who examined the record
options.D: A copy of the whole record, with the exempt portion marked on it

e: Section 7(8) of the RTI Act, 2005 requires the CPIO, on rejecting a request, to communicate the reasons for rejection, the period within which an appeal may be preferred, and the particulars of the appellate authority.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 27 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 52,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: 27 years give 54 six-monthly periods; retirement gratuity is 1/4 x emoluments per period, that is 54 x 1/4 = 13.5 months of emoluments. Computation: 13.5 x Rs 52,000 = Rs 7,02,000.

q: Under Section 17 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every part of a factory where workers are working or passing, there shall be provided and maintained:

options.A: Air-conditioning throughout the year
options.B: Sufficient and suitable lighting, natural or artificial, or both
options.C: Only artificial lighting, natural light being excluded
options.D: Lighting only during the night shift

e: Section 17 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires sufficient and suitable lighting, natural or artificial or both, in every part of a factory where workers are working or passing.

q: Under Section 4 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, an application for registration of a trade union of railway servants may be made by:

options.A: Any seven or more members of the trade union, by subscribing their names to the rules of the union and complying with the provisions of the Act
options.B: Only the General Secretary of a recognised federation
options.C: Not less than one hundred members of the union in every case
options.D: The General Manager of the Railway alone

e: Section 4 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 permits an application for registration to be made by any seven or more members of the union, by subscribing their names to the rules of the union and complying with the provisions of the Act.

q: Under Section 18 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every Authority appointed under the Act for hearing claims shall have, for the purposes of taking evidence, administering oaths, enforcing the attendance of witnesses and compelling the production of documents, all the powers of:

options.A: A criminal court trying an offence under the Indian Penal Code
options.B: The Central Administrative Tribunal
options.C: A departmental Inquiring Authority
options.D: A civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure

e: Section 18 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 gives every Authority under the Act, for taking evidence, administering oaths, enforcing attendance of witnesses and compelling production of documents, all the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure.

q: Under Section 60 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in any factory:

options.A: On a weekly holiday in any circumstances
options.B: In a shift which extends beyond eight hours
options.C: On any day on which he has already been working in another factory, except in the circumstances prescribed in this behalf
options.D: In more than one section of the same factory on the same day

e: Section 60 of the Factories Act, 1948 provides that no adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in any factory on any day on which he has already been working in another factory, except in the circumstances prescribed in that behalf.

q: Post-retirement complimentary passes admissible to a retired railway servant of Group 'C' with 25 years or more of service are issued at the rate of:

options.A: One set of passes per year
options.B: Two sets of passes per year
options.C: Three sets of passes per year
options.D: Six sets of passes per year

e: Under the Railway Servants (Pass) Rules, post-retirement complimentary passes for a retired Group C railway servant with the prescribed long service, including 25 years or more, are issued at two sets per year.

q: Under Section 15 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the State Information Commission consists of:

options.A: The State Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten State Information Commissioners
options.B: The State Chief Information Commissioner and not more than five State Information Commissioners
options.C: The State Chief Information Commissioner alone
options.D: The State Chief Information Commissioner and exactly ten State Information Commissioners

e: Section 15 of the RTI Act, 2005 constitutes the State Information Commission with the State Chief Information Commissioner and such number of State Information Commissioners, not exceeding ten, as may be deemed necessary.

q: Under Section 33 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, every fixed vessel, sump, tank, pit or opening in the ground or in a floor, which, by reason of its depth, situation, construction or contents, is or may be a source of danger, shall be:

options.A: Merely marked with a red line around it
options.B: Filled up with earth in every case
options.C: Kept locked by the foreman of the shop
options.D: Either securely covered or securely fenced

e: Section 33 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires every fixed vessel, sump, tank, pit or opening which may be a source of danger by reason of its depth, situation, construction or contents to be either securely covered or securely fenced.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 58,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 29,000 per month
options.B: Rs 17,400 per month
options.C: Rs 11,600 per month
options.D: Rs 23,200 per month

e: Normal family pension is 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn. Computation: 30 per cent of Rs 58,000 = Rs 17,400 per month.

q: The cash equivalent of leave salary received by a railway servant, a Government employee, at the time of his retirement, in respect of the earned leave at his credit, is, under the Income-tax Act:

options.A: Fully taxable as income from salaries
options.B: Exempt only to the extent of Rs 3,00,000
options.C: Fully exempt from income tax
options.D: Exempt only to the extent of Rs 25,00,000

e: Cash equivalent of leave salary for earned leave at credit received by a Government employee at retirement is fully exempt under Section 10(10AA)(i) of the Income-tax Act, 1961; the monetary ceiling applies only to non-Government employees.

q: Under Section 27 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no woman or child shall be employed:

options.A: In any part of a factory for pressing cotton in which a cotton-opener is at work
options.B: In the office rooms of a factory
options.C: In a factory during the day shift
options.D: In a factory in which power is used

e: Section 27 of the Factories Act, 1948 prohibits employment of any woman or child in any part of a factory for pressing cotton in which a cotton-opener is at work, because of the danger from the open machinery.

q: Under Section 18(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the Central Information Commission may receive and inquire into a complaint from a person who:

options.A: Is dissatisfied with the grading in his Annual Performance Appraisal Report
options.B: Seeks a transfer to a station of his choice
options.C: Has been transferred from one Railway to another
options.D: Has been unable to submit a request for information because no Central Public Information Officer has been designated in the public authority

e: Section 18(1) of the RTI Act, 2005 empowers the Central Information Commission to receive and inquire into a complaint from a person who has been unable to submit a request because no CPIO has been designated in the public authority, among other grounds.

q: Under Section 9 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, an Inspector of Factories may, within the local limits for which he is appointed:

options.A: Impose any penalty on a worker employed in the factory
options.B: Enter and inspect, at any time during working hours, with such assistants as he thinks fit, any place which is used, or which he has reason to believe is used, as a factory
options.C: Cancel the licence of the factory on the spot
options.D: Order the dismissal of the manager of the factory

e: Section 9 of the Factories Act, 1948 empowers an Inspector, within his local limits, to enter and inspect at any time during working hours, with assistants, any place used or believed to be used as a factory.

q: Under Section 8 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, compensation payable in respect of the death of an employee, and any lump sum payable to a woman or a person under a legal disability, shall be paid:

options.A: Directly by the employer to the dependent in cash
options.B: Through the recognised trade union of the establishment
options.C: By deposit with the Commissioner for employees' compensation, a payment otherwise than by such deposit not being deemed to be a payment of compensation
options.D: Only after the retirement benefits of the deceased are settled

e: Section 8 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 requires compensation for death, and lump sums payable to a woman or a person under legal disability, to be paid by deposit with the Commissioner; payment otherwise than by such deposit is not deemed payment of compensation.

q: Personal Computer Advance admissible to a railway servant is recovered from him in monthly instalments not exceeding:
e: Personal Computer Advance admissible to a railway servant is recovered in monthly instalments not exceeding 150, under the General Financial and advance rules applied on the Railways.

q: Under Section 58 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, where work in a factory is carried on by a system of shifts, the system of shifts shall be so arranged that:

options.A: Every worker works in two shifts on the same day
options.B: The shifts are changed every day of the week
options.C: Workers are transferred from one shift to another without any notice
options.D: There is no overlapping of shifts

e: Section 58 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires that where work is carried on by a system of shifts, the system shall be so arranged that there is no overlapping of shifts.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 8 months of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 70,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at two times the emoluments, as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death after 8 months, that is less than one year, falls in the lowest slab, so death gratuity is 2 x emoluments under the RS (Pension) Rules. Computation: 2 x Rs 70,000 = Rs 1,40,000.

q: Under Section 16 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, a registered trade union of railway servants may constitute a separate political fund for the promotion of the civic and political interests of its members. In regard to contributions to that fund, the correct position is that:

options.A: Every member is compelled to contribute to the fund
options.B: The fund is met wholly from the general funds of the union
options.C: A member is not under any obligation to contribute to the fund, and a member who does not contribute cannot be excluded from the benefits of the union on that ground
options.D: Contributions to the fund are recovered from the wages of all members by the employer

e: Section 16 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 keeps the political fund separate and voluntary: no member is under any obligation to contribute to it, and a non-contributing member cannot be excluded from the benefits of the union on that ground.

q: Under Section 14 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, where, in any factory, any exhaust dust, fume or other impurity of a nature likely to be injurious to the health of the workers is given off, effective measures shall be taken to prevent its inhalation and accumulation, and an exhaust appliance shall be applied:

options.A: As near as possible to the point of origin of the dust, fume or other impurity
options.B: Only at the main gate of the factory
options.C: Only in the office rooms of the factory
options.D: At a distance of one hundred metres from the workroom

e: Section 14 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires effective measures against inhalation and accumulation of exhaust dust, fume or impurity, with the exhaust appliance applied as near as possible to the point of origin of the impurity.

q: Under Section 12(6) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the Chief Information Commissioner and an Information Commissioner shall not:

options.A: Hold office for more than one term in any case
options.B: Be appointed from among persons of eminence in public life
options.C: Draw a salary from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Be a Member of Parliament or of the Legislature of any State, hold any other office of profit, be connected with any political party, or carry on any business or pursue any profession

e: Section 12(6) of the RTI Act, 2005 disqualifies the CIC and Information Commissioners from being a Member of Parliament or of a State Legislature, holding any other office of profit, being connected with a political party, or carrying on any business or profession.

q: A railway servant who is summoned to give evidence, in his official capacity, in a departmental inquiry or in a court, in a case to which the Government is a party, is entitled, for the journey performed by him for that purpose, to:

options.A: No travelling allowance of any kind
options.B: Travelling allowance as admissible to him for a journey on tour, the period of his attendance being treated as on duty
options.C: Only a fixed witness fee of Rs 100 per day
options.D: Leave without pay for the period of his attendance

e: A railway servant summoned to give evidence in his official capacity in a departmental inquiry or court in a case to which Government is a party gets Travelling Allowance as for a journey on tour, and his attendance period is treated as on duty.

q: Under Section 30 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a notice indicating the maximum safe working peripheral speed of every grindstone or abrasive wheel, and the safe working speed of the corresponding spindle affected thereby, shall be:

options.A: Recorded only in the muster roll of the factory
options.B: Communicated orally to the workers by the foreman
options.C: Fixed permanently on or near the grindstone or abrasive wheel, and near the corresponding spindle
options.D: Sent to the Accounts Office of the Railway every year

e: Section 30 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires a notice indicating the maximum safe working peripheral speed of every grindstone or abrasive wheel and the safe speed of the corresponding spindle to be fixed permanently on or near the wheel and the spindle.

q: Under Section 22 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, no court shall entertain any suit for the recovery of wages, or of any deduction from wages, in so far as:

options.A: The sum so claimed could have been recovered by an application to the Authority under Section 15 of the Act, or has been the subject of such an application or of a direction thereon
options.B: The employed person is a member of a recognised trade union
options.C: The employed person has completed five years of service
options.D: The wages claimed relate to a period of more than one month

e: Section 22 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 bars a civil suit for recovery of wages or deductions so far as the sum claimed could have been recovered by an application to the Authority under Section 15, or has been the subject of such an application or direction.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 4 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 58,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: With 4 years and no pension entitlement, service gratuity is half a month's emoluments per six-monthly period. 4 years give 8 periods, that is 8 x 1/2 = 4 months. Computation: 4 x Rs 58,000 = Rs 2,32,000.

q: Where a factory is exempted, under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, from the provisions relating to weekly hours, daily hours and intervals for rest, the total hours of work of a worker in any week, including the overtime work done by him, shall not exceed:

options.A: Forty-eight hours
options.B: Sixty hours
options.C: Seventy-two hours
options.D: Eighty-four hours

e: Where a factory is exempted from the weekly hours, daily hours and rest interval provisions, Section 65 of the Factories Act, 1948 still caps the total hours of work in any week, including overtime, at sixty hours.

q: Under Section 19(7) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the decision of the Central Information Commission, in an appeal decided by it, shall be:

options.A: Only recommendatory in nature
options.B: Binding only on the applicant
options.C: Binding
options.D: Binding only if it is confirmed by the Central Government

e: Section 19(7) of the RTI Act, 2005 states in plain terms that the decision of the Central Information Commission shall be binding, and it is not merely recommendatory or subject to confirmation by the Central Government.

q: Under Section 34 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no person shall be employed in any factory to lift, carry or move any load:

options.A: So heavy as to be likely to cause him injury
options.B: Weighing more than one kilogram
options.C: Without the assistance of another worker in every case
options.D: During the night shift in any circumstances

e: Section 34 of the Factories Act, 1948 provides that no person shall be employed in any factory to lift, carry or move any load so heavy as to be likely to cause him injury.

q: Under the Apprenticeship Rules made under the Apprentices Act, 1961, a trade apprentice engaged on the Railways is entitled, during the period of his apprenticeship training, to casual leave of:

options.A: 30 days in a year
options.B: 20 days in a year
options.C: 8 days in a year
options.D: 12 days in a year

e: Under the Apprenticeship Rules under the Apprentices Act, 1961, a trade apprentice is entitled during his apprenticeship training to casual leave of 12 days in a year, apart from the prescribed medical and extraordinary leave.

q: Under Section 108 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the abstracts of the Act and of the rules made thereunder, in the prescribed form, shall be displayed in every factory:

options.A: Only in the English language, whatever be the language of the workers
options.B: Only in the record room of the factory
options.C: Only when the Inspector of Factories so directs in writing
options.D: In English and in a language understood by the majority of the workers employed in the factory, together with the name and address of the Inspector and of the certifying surgeon

e: Section 108 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the abstracts of the Act and rules to be displayed in English and in a language understood by the majority of the workers, together with the name and address of the Inspector and the certifying surgeon.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 62,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate, at 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 18,600 per month
options.B: Rs 24,800 per month
options.C: Rs 31,000 per month
options.D: Rs 46,500 per month

e: Enhanced family pension is 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn. Computation: 50 per cent of Rs 62,000 = Rs 31,000 per month.

q: Under Section 118A of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, an Inspector of Factories shall treat as absolutely confidential:

options.A: The source of any complaint regarding the contravention of any provision of the Act, and shall give no intimation to the occupier or his representative that the inspection was made in consequence of the receipt of such a complaint
options.B: The name of the occupier of the factory
options.C: The number of workers employed in the factory
options.D: The abstracts of the Act displayed in the factory

e: Section 118A of the Factories Act, 1948 obliges an Inspector to treat as absolutely confidential the source of any complaint about contravention of the Act, and to give no intimation to the occupier that the inspection followed such a complaint.

q: Under Section 6(2) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, an applicant making a request for information shall:

options.A: State the reasons for seeking the information
options.B: Not be required to give any reason for requesting the information, or any other personal detail except those that may be necessary for contacting him
options.C: Prove that the information is required in public interest
options.D: Disclose the source from which he learnt of the record

e: Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, 2005 provides that an applicant shall not be required to give any reason for requesting the information, or any personal detail other than those necessary for contacting him.

q: Under Section 15 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every factory there shall be provided:

options.A: Washing facilities only for male workers
options.B: Washing facilities only in factories employing more than 500 workers
options.C: Adequate and suitable washing facilities, separately for the use of male and female workers, maintained in a clean condition
options.D: Washing facilities only if the occupier considers them necessary

e: Section 15 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires adequate and suitable washing facilities in every factory, provided separately for the use of male and female workers and maintained in a clean condition.

q: Under Rule 15 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to private trade or employment, a railway servant shall not, except with the previous sanction of the prescribed authority:

options.A: Engage directly or indirectly in any trade or business, or undertake any other employment
options.B: Purchase household goods from a private trader
options.C: Open a savings bank account in a nationalised bank
options.D: Reside in a house owned by a private person

e: Rule 15 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 bars a railway servant, except with the previous sanction of the prescribed authority, from engaging directly or indirectly in any trade or business or undertaking any other employment.

q: Under Section 13 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, every trade union of railway servants which is registered under the Act shall be:

options.A: A department of the Railway Administration
options.B: An unincorporated association of its members
options.C: A society registered under the Societies Registration Act
options.D: A body corporate, having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire and hold property

e: Section 13 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 makes every registered trade union a body corporate by the name under which it is registered, with perpetual succession and a common seal and power to acquire and hold property.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 3 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 52,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at six times the emoluments, as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death after 3 years falls in the 1-5 years slab, so death gratuity is 6 x emoluments under the RS (Pension) Rules. Computation: 6 x Rs 52,000 = Rs 3,12,000.

q: Under Section 5 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where an employee has been in the service of his employer for a period of not less than twelve months preceding an accident, his monthly wages, for the purpose of computing compensation, shall be deemed to be:

options.A: The wages payable to him for the month in which the accident occurred
options.B: One-sixth of the total wages earned by him in the preceding twelve months
options.C: One-twelfth of the total wages which have fallen due for payment to him in the preceding twelve months
options.D: The minimum wages notified for his category of employment

e: Section 5 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 deems the monthly wages of an employee in service for not less than twelve months preceding the accident to be one-twelfth of the total wages fallen due in those preceding twelve months.

q: A female railway servant avails Child Care Leave for the full period of 730 days. The leave salary admissible to her during the next 365 days of such leave, after the first 365 days, is:

options.A: The full pay admissible to her
options.B: 80 per cent of the pay admissible to her
options.C: 50 per cent of the pay admissible to her
options.D: Equal to the leave salary admissible on Leave on Half Average Pay

e: For Child Care Leave, the first 365 days carry full leave salary and the next 365 days carry leave salary at 80 per cent of the pay admissible, so a servant availing the full 730 days gets 80 per cent in the second block of 365 days.

q: Under Section 19(3) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, a second appeal against the decision of the First Appellate Authority shall lie to the Central Information Commission within:

options.A: 30 days from the date on which the decision should have been made or was actually received
options.B: 45 days from the date on which the decision should have been made or was actually received
options.C: 60 days from the date on which the decision should have been made or was actually received
options.D: 90 days from the date on which the decision should have been made or was actually received

e: Section 19(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 provides that a second appeal against the First Appellate Authority's decision lies to the Central Information Commission within 90 days from the date the decision should have been made or was actually received.

q: Under Section 22 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the examination of any part of machinery while it is in motion, and any operation incidental thereto, shall be made or carried out only by:

options.A: A specially trained adult male worker wearing tight-fitting clothing provided by the occupier
options.B: The foreman of the shop personally
options.C: A worker who has put in at least ten years of service
options.D: An apprentice working under supervision

e: Section 22 of the Factories Act, 1948 restricts examination of machinery in motion and incidental operations to a specially trained adult male worker wearing tight-fitting clothing provided by the occupier.

q: Under Rule 18 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not, except with the previous sanction of the prescribed authority, in his own name or in the name of any member of his family:

options.A: Accept any gift on a ceremonial occasion
options.B: Make an investment in Government securities
options.C: Acquire or dispose of any immovable property by lease, mortgage, purchase, sale or gift
options.D: Submit his annual immovable property return

e: Rule 18 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 requires a railway servant, except with the previous sanction of the prescribed authority, not to acquire or dispose of any immovable property by lease, mortgage, purchase, sale or gift in his own or a family member's name.

q: Under Section 22 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, in the case of a registered trade union of railway servants, not less than the following proportion of the total number of office-bearers shall be persons actually engaged or employed in the industry with which the trade union is connected:

options.A: One-third
options.B: One-half
options.C: Two-thirds
options.D: Three-fourths

e: Section 22 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 requires that not less than one-half of the total office-bearers of a registered trade union shall be persons actually engaged or employed in the industry with which the union is connected.

q: Under Section 12 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where an employer, in the course of or for the purpose of his business, contracts with a contractor for the execution of any work, and an employee employed by the contractor sustains personal injury by accident, the compensation shall in the first instance be payable by:

options.A: The contractor alone, the principal employer having no liability
options.B: The Commissioner for Employees' Compensation
options.C: The employee's trade union
options.D: The principal employer, who shall be entitled to be indemnified by the contractor

e: Section 12 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 makes the principal employer liable in the first instance to pay compensation for a contractor's employee injured in work contracted for his business, with a right to be indemnified by the contractor.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 24 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 47,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: 24 years give 48 six-monthly periods; retirement gratuity is 1/4 x emoluments per period, that is 48 x 1/4 = 12 months of emoluments. Computation: 12 x Rs 47,000 = Rs 5,64,000.

q: Under Section 3 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, subject to the provisions of the Act, the right to information is available to:

options.A: All citizens
options.B: All persons, including companies and firms
options.C: All residents of India, whether citizens or not
options.D: Only persons who are not Government servants

e: Section 3 of the RTI Act, 2005 confers the right to information, subject to the provisions of the Act, on all citizens. It is a citizen's right and does not extend to all persons, companies or firms as such.

q: Under Section 38 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every factory, all practicable measures shall be taken to prevent the outbreak of fire and its spread, and in particular:

options.A: Workers shall not be permitted to leave the factory until the fire is extinguished
options.B: Doors of the factory shall be kept locked during working hours
options.C: Fire-fighting equipment shall be kept under the personal custody of the manager
options.D: Doors affording exit in case of fire shall not be so locked or fastened that they cannot be easily and immediately opened from inside

e: Section 38 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires all practicable fire precautions, and in particular that doors affording exit in case of fire shall not be so locked or fastened that they cannot be easily and immediately opened from inside.

q: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, whenever the Dearness Allowance payable to railway servants increases by 50 per cent, the rates of allowances such as Children Education Allowance and Hostel Subsidy stand increased by:

options.A: 10 per cent
options.B: 25 per cent
options.C: 50 per cent
options.D: No increase is admissible

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, whenever Dearness Allowance increases by 50 per cent, the rates of allowances such as Children Education Allowance and Hostel Subsidy are increased by 25 per cent.

q: Under Rule 11 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to unauthorised communication of information, a railway servant shall not, except in accordance with any general or special order of the Government or in the performance in good faith of the duties assigned to him:

options.A: Read any official document in the course of his duties
options.B: Consult his immediate superior on an official matter
options.C: Communicate, directly or indirectly, any official document or any part thereof, or information, to any person to whom he is not authorised to communicate it
options.D: Maintain the records of his office in the prescribed manner

e: Rule 11 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 bars a railway servant, except under a general or special Government order or in good faith performance of his duties, from communicating any official document or information to a person he is not authorised to communicate it to.

q: Under the Apprentices Act, 1961, any dispute arising between an employer and an apprentice out of the contract of apprenticeship, such as that of an Act Apprentice engaged in a railway workshop, shall be referred for decision to:

options.A: The Apprenticeship Adviser
options.B: The Labour Court
options.C: The District Judge
options.D: The Railway Rates Tribunal

e: Under the Apprentices Act, 1961, any dispute between an employer and an apprentice arising out of the contract of apprenticeship is referred for decision to the Apprenticeship Adviser, not to a labour court or civil court.

q: Under the 7th CPC pay structure, an annual increment is admissible to a railway servant on 1st January or 1st July, as the case may be, only where he has rendered, as on that date, service in the level concerned of not less than:

options.A: Three months
options.B: One month
options.C: Twelve months
options.D: Six months

e: Under the 7th CPC pay structure, an annual increment on 1st January or 1st July is admissible only where the railway servant has rendered, as on that date, not less than six months of service in the level concerned.

q: Under Section 32 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every factory:

options.A: Floors and passages may be used for the storage of material
options.B: Floors, steps, stairs, passages and gangways shall be of sound construction and properly maintained, and shall be kept free from obstructions and substances likely to cause persons to slip
options.C: Stairs and gangways are required only in multi-storeyed buildings
options.D: Passages shall be washed once in a year

e: Section 32 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires floors, steps, stairs, passages and gangways to be of sound construction, properly maintained, and kept free from obstructions and substances likely to cause persons to slip.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 54,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate, at 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 27,000 per month
options.B: Rs 16,200 per month
options.C: Rs 54,000 per month
options.D: Rs 21,600 per month

e: Enhanced family pension is 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn. Computation: 50 per cent of Rs 54,000 = Rs 27,000 per month.

q: Under Section 11 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, where a Central Public Information Officer intends to disclose information supplied by a third party and treated as confidential by that third party, he shall, after giving the third party an opportunity of making a representation, make a decision on the disclosure within:

options.A: 30 days from the receipt of the request for information
options.B: 60 days from the receipt of the request for information
options.C: 40 days from the receipt of the request for information
options.D: 15 days from the receipt of the request for information

e: Section 11 of the RTI Act, 2005 requires the CPIO who intends to disclose third-party confidential information, after giving the third party an opportunity of representation, to decide on disclosure within 40 days from receipt of the request.

q: Under Section 21 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, a person shall be entitled to be a member of a registered trade union of railway servants, and to enjoy the privileges of a member, if he has attained the age of:

options.A: 18 years
options.B: 21 years
options.C: 16 years
options.D: 15 years

e: Section 21 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 entitles a person who has attained the age of 15 years to be a member of a registered trade union and to enjoy the privileges of a member, subject to the rules of the union.

q: Under Section 17 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, any contract or agreement whereby an employee relinquishes any right of compensation from his employer for personal injury arising out of and in the course of his employment shall be:

options.A: Valid if it is registered with the Commissioner
options.B: Null and void, in so far as it purports to remove or reduce the liability of any person to pay compensation under the Act
options.C: Valid with the prior approval of the State Government
options.D: Enforceable only against the employee

e: Section 17 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 makes any contract or agreement by which an employee relinquishes his right to compensation null and void, so far as it purports to remove or reduce the employer's liability under the Act.

q: House Building Advance is admissible to a railway servant:

options.A: Only once during the entire period of his service
options.B: Once in every ten years of his service
options.C: Any number of times, provided the earlier advance has been fully repaid
options.D: Twice during his service, once for purchase of a plot and once for construction

e: House Building Advance is admissible to a railway servant only once during the entire period of his service, under the HBA rules, whether for purchase, construction or enlargement as permitted in that single grant.

q: Under Section 41G of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the occupier shall set up a Safety Committee, consisting of equal number of representatives of workers and the management, in every factory:

options.A: Wherein 100 or more workers are ordinarily employed
options.B: Wherein a canteen is required to be maintained
options.C: Wherein a hazardous process is carried on, or wherein hazardous substances are used or handled
options.D: Which is declared to be a workshop of the Railways

e: Section 41G of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the occupier to set up a Safety Committee with equal worker and management representatives in every factory wherein a hazardous process is carried on or hazardous substances are used or handled.

q: Fixed Travelling Allowance is granted to a railway servant:

options.A: For journeys performed by him on transfer
options.B: In lieu of the mileage allowance for journeys by road
options.C: As a fixed monthly amount in lieu of travelling allowance for official journeys within his headquarters town
options.D: Whose duties require him to travel extensively within a specified area or jurisdiction, in lieu of daily allowance for such journeys

e: Fixed Travelling Allowance is granted as a fixed monthly amount to a railway servant whose duties require him to travel extensively within a specified area or jurisdiction, in lieu of daily allowance for such journeys.

q: Joining time which is admissible to a railway servant on transfer in public interest, but is not availed of by him, is credited to his Leave on Average Pay account, subject to a maximum of:

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 20 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 15 days

e: Joining time admissible on transfer in public interest but not availed of is credited to the Leave on Average Pay account of the railway servant, subject to a maximum of 15 days, under the joining time rules.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 8 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 51,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: With 8 years and no pension entitlement, service gratuity is half a month's emoluments per six-monthly period. 8 years give 16 periods, that is 16 x 1/2 = 8 months. Computation: 8 x Rs 51,000 = Rs 4,08,000.

q: A railway servant who is arrested on a criminal charge, or is detained in custody for a period exceeding forty-eight hours, is required to:

options.A: Report the fact of his arrest and detention to his immediate official superior as soon as possible
options.B: Resign from service forthwith
options.C: Report the matter only if he is convicted by the court
options.D: Inform the Railway Board directly in all cases

e: A railway servant arrested on a criminal charge or detained in custody for more than forty-eight hours must report the fact of his arrest and detention to his immediate official superior as soon as possible, under the Conduct and service instructions.

q: In regard to commutation of family pension admissible to the family of a deceased railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: Up to 40 per cent of the family pension can be commuted
options.B: Up to 20 per cent of the family pension can be commuted
options.C: Family pension cannot be commuted for a lump sum payment
options.D: Family pension can be commuted only with the sanction of the Railway Board

e: Commutation for a lump sum is a facility available only on the pension of the retired railway servant himself. Family pension admissible to the family of a deceased railway servant cannot be commuted for a lump sum payment.

q: Under Section 7(3) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, where a decision is taken to provide information on payment of any further fee representing the cost of providing the information, the period intervening between the dispatch of the intimation regarding the further fee and the payment of the fee by the applicant shall:

options.A: Be counted within the period of thirty days prescribed for providing the information
options.B: Be excluded in calculating the period of thirty days prescribed for providing the information
options.C: Render the request liable to be rejected
options.D: Be treated as a period of deemed refusal of the request

e: Section 7(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 provides that where information is to be supplied on payment of further fee, the period between dispatch of the fee intimation and payment of the fee by the applicant is excluded in calculating the thirty-day period.

q: Under Section 4 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where death results from an injury sustained by an employee arising out of and in the course of his employment, the minimum amount of compensation payable to his dependants is:
e: Section 4 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 fixes, where death results from the injury, compensation at 50 per cent of monthly wages times the relevant factor or Rs 1,20,000, whichever is more, so Rs 1,20,000 is the statutory minimum for death.

q: The services of a non-gazetted railway servant who is on probation may be terminated by the appointing authority during the period of probation, without assigning any reason, by:

options.A: Giving him three months' notice in writing
options.B: Giving him six months' notice in writing
options.C: Holding a full departmental inquiry against him
options.D: Giving him one month's notice in writing, or pay in lieu thereof

e: During probation, the services of a non-gazetted railway servant may be terminated by the appointing authority without assigning any reason by giving him one month's notice in writing, or pay in lieu thereof, under the service rules.

q: The monthly pension, that is, the uncommuted pension, received by a retired railway servant is, under the Income-tax Act:

options.A: Fully taxable as income under the head 'Salaries'
options.B: Fully exempt from income-tax
options.C: Taxable only if it exceeds Rs 50,000 per month
options.D: Taxable under the head 'Income from other sources' only

e: The monthly uncommuted pension received by a retired railway servant is fully taxable as income under the head Salaries under the Income-tax Act; only the commuted value of pension enjoys exemption for Government employees.

q: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, the periodical rest admissible to running staff at their headquarters in a calendar month shall be:

options.A: Two periods of not less than 24 consecutive hours each
options.B: At least four periods of rest of not less than 30 consecutive hours each, or five periods of rest of not less than 22 consecutive hours each
options.C: One period of not less than 48 consecutive hours
options.D: A weekly rest of 30 consecutive hours, as in the case of 'Continuous' staff

e: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, running staff get periodical rest at headquarters of at least four periods of not less than 30 consecutive hours each, or five periods of not less than 22 consecutive hours each, in a calendar month.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 22 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 49,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Death after 22 years falls in the 20 years and above slab: half a month's emoluments per six-monthly period. 22 years give 44 periods, that is 44 x 1/2 = 22 months, within the 33 x maximum. Computation: 22 x Rs 49,000 = Rs 10,78,000.

q: Recruitment to posts on a zonal Railway against the Scouts and Guides quota is ordinarily made in a year to the extent of:

options.A: Five posts in Level-1 and five posts in Level-2
options.B: One post in Level-1 only
options.C: Two posts in Level-2 per Railway per year and two posts in Level-1 per Division per year
options.D: Ten posts in Level-1 and ten posts in Level-2

e: Recruitment against the Scouts and Guides quota is ordinarily two posts in Level-2 per Railway per year and two posts in Level-1 per Division per year, under the Railway Board's quota instructions.

q: In the selection for the post of Assistant Financial Adviser through the Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, the marks allotted to the viva-voce and to the record of service of the candidate are, respectively:

options.A: 25 marks and 25 marks
options.B: 50 marks and 50 marks
options.C: 25 marks and 50 marks
options.D: 10 marks and 15 marks

e: In the LDCE selection for Assistant Financial Adviser, the viva-voce carries 25 marks and the record of service carries 25 marks, the balance of the total being for the written examination.

q: In the Service Book of a non-gazetted railway servant, the entries relating to his suspension and to the punishments awarded to him are recorded:

options.A: In pencil, so that they can be erased later
options.B: Only in the confidential report dossier
options.C: In a separate register maintained by the Accounts Office
options.D: In red ink

e: In the Service Book of a non-gazetted railway servant, entries relating to his suspension and to punishments awarded to him are recorded in red ink, so that they stand out from the ordinary entries.

q: On the grant of a financial upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression scheme, the pay of a railway servant in the higher level is fixed by:

options.A: Granting him two increments in his existing level
options.B: Granting him one increment in his existing level and thereafter placing him in the higher level at the cell equal to the amount so arrived at, or the next cell above it, in that level
options.C: Fixing his pay at the minimum of the higher level in all cases
options.D: Granting him a personal pay equal to one increment, without a change of level

e: On MACP financial upgradation, pay is fixed by granting one increment in the existing level and then placing the servant in the higher level at the cell equal to the amount so arrived at, or the next cell above it, in that level.

q: Where a railway servant dies while in service without making a nomination for Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity, and he has also not left behind him any member of his family, the gratuity payable in respect of him shall:

options.A: Be paid to his legal heir on production of a succession certificate in all cases
options.B: Be credited to the Staff Benefit Fund
options.C: Lapse to the Government
options.D: Be kept in deposit indefinitely

e: Where a railway servant dies in service without a nomination for DCRG and leaves no family member behind, the gratuity payable in respect of him lapses to the Government under the RS (Pension) Rules.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 64,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 19,200 per month
options.B: Rs 32,000 per month
options.C: Rs 12,800 per month
options.D: Rs 25,600 per month

e: Normal family pension is 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn. Computation: 30 per cent of Rs 64,000 = Rs 19,200 per month.

q: A widow pass admissible to the widow of a deceased railway servant is issued at the rate of:

options.A: The same number of sets as was admissible to the deceased railway servant as post-retirement complimentary passes
options.B: Half the number of sets of post-retirement complimentary passes admissible to the deceased railway servant, subject to a minimum of one set in alternate years
options.C: One set only, during the whole period of her widowhood
options.D: Two sets in every calendar year, irrespective of the entitlement of the deceased

e: A widow pass is issued to the widow of a deceased railway servant at half the number of sets of post-retirement complimentary passes admissible to the deceased, subject to a minimum of one set in alternate years, under the Pass Rules.

q: Under Section 135B of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every person employed in any business, trade or industrial undertaking, who is entitled to vote at an election to the House of the People or to the Legislative Assembly of a State, shall, on the day for polling:

options.A: Be granted leave without pay for the day
options.B: Be required to work for half a day before proceeding to vote
options.C: Be granted a holiday only if he produces proof of having voted
options.D: Be granted a holiday on that day, and no deduction shall be made from his wages on account of such holiday

e: Section 135B of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 requires every employed person entitled to vote to be granted a holiday on the polling day, and no deduction or abatement of wages shall be made on account of that holiday.
